text:
alex_c: FYI Novara just opened a ticket — p99 spikes and occasional 503s on /v1/generate for tenant novara-prod since ~09:10. They see user-facing timeouts, customers hitting retry loops. Requesting urgent help :fire_engine:

novara_ops: cc @alex_c — yes we're getting alerts from our side. We've collected some request IDs: 8f3a2b1c, 8f3a2b5f, 8f3a2c01. Spikes align with a specific workflow that sends many short requests in parallel.

alex_c: attaching the customer's partial curl and a few logs they pasted:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -d '{"model":"xlarge-v2","inputs":[...],"max_tokens":64}'

[LOG] request_id=8f3a2b1c tenant=novara-prod route=/v1/generate latency=138ms status=200
[LOG] request_id=8f3a2b5f tenant=novara-prod route=/v1/generate latency=135ms status=502
[LOG] request_id=8f3a2c01 tenant=novara-prod queue_wait_ms=2600 worker_wait_ms=2200 status=504
```

maya_oncall: :eyes: can someone pull tenant_queue_depth and tenant_worker_wait histograms for novara-prod across the last 30m? also paste any p95/p99 traces if available.

sam_sre: grabbing metrics now. Quick note — we saw a cluster-level KV cache eviction storm earlier due to long contexts from another tenant; could be noisy neighbor or queue head-of-line blocking.

sam_sre: metrics (summary): tenant_queue_depth: spike to 42 at 09:12. worker_wait_ms p95 ~ 820ms p99 ~ 2.2s. Overall host CPU/GPU not saturated but one node shows high epoll wait.

jules_eng: that pattern (queue_depth + head-of-line waits) often happens when a tenant fires many concurrent short requests and the scheduler sticks them onto same worker. Are they on shared pool or reserved?

novara_ops: shared pool. We didn't reserve capacity — current cost concerns.

ryan_prod: we have an emergency mitigation path: 1) short-term: add tenant to per-tenant burst reservation/bespoke allowlist so their requests route to a reserved burst lane (pre-provisioned), 2) medium: recommend pinning them to a dedicated small reservation, 3) long-term: SRE tune scheduler to avoid head-of-line blocking for high concurrency short requests.

alex_c: Novara asked if we can do immediate allowlist/exempt from the per-tenant concurrency throttle for a few minutes while they investigate. Is that feasible?

sam_sre: yes — we can flip a per-tenant bypass flag in rate-limiter. Quick command (internal):

```
# add tenant to throttle bypass (ephemeral)
redwoodctl tenant update --id novara-prod --set throttle_bypass=true --expiry 15m
```

sam_sre: toggling now for a 15m window while we monitor. will post results.

deploy-bot: ETA: change submitted by sam_sre, change-id=chg_2026_177500. Applying in 2s... applied.

jules_eng: while bypass is on, we still need to watch N+1 effects — if they flood shared workers we'll degrade other tenants. Recommend also enabling request shaping (limit per-worker concurrency) and enabling KV cache warming for their common prefixes.

novara_ops: thank you — seeing immediate improvement in response rates. p99 dropped from ~2.2s to ~320ms within 90s. Still seeing occasional 5xxs but much better.

maya_oncall: can we surface a short RCA plan to Novara: cause hypothesis (shared-pool queue head-of-line caused by high parallel short requests + partial KV cache evictions), mitigation applied (15m throttle_bypass), follow-ups (recommend pinning small reservation or scheduled burst window), and ask for their typical qps patterns?

ryan_prod: i'll draft an email and include suggested config options and cost estimates for a small dedicated reservation (slot of 2x A100-equivalent for expected qps) + burst buffer.

sam_sre: follow-up technical items: 1) collect full trace for request_ids above, 2) add per-tenant queue depth alert at lower threshold (now 20 -> set to 10 for shared tenants), 3) create repro load test (simulate many short 50-80ms requests) on a staging cluster to validate scheduler changes.

alex_c: Novara wants the bypass extended to 2 hours while they re-run their rollout. They also asked whether we can add specific allowlist for a known IP range (their proxy) to avoid rate-limit at edge.

jules_eng: IP allowlist at the edge is doable — that's an ingress rule. But that bypasses some of our global rate-limiting so need legal/risks signoff for extended window. For now we can extend to 2h under monitoring. Commands:

```
# extend bypass to 2 hours
redwoodctl tenant update --id novara-prod --set throttle_bypass=true --expiry 120m
# add IP allowlist for tenant
redwoodctl network allowlist add --tenant novara-prod --cidr 52.17.12.0/24 --reason "customer proxy"
```

novara_ops: please do extend and add the IP range. We'll provide SOC contacts for compliance.

maya_oncall: safety checklist before extending: enable per-host backpressure, set soft-fallback to lower-cap models if queue depth rises >30, and add alert if other tenants' p99 increases by >20%.

sam_sre: done: extended bypass to 2h, added allowlist entry. change-id=chg_2026_177501. Monitoring dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/tenants/novara-prod

deploy-bot: change applied.

alex_c: Novara confirms improved stability. They'll run their rollout in the next 90m and report.

ryan_prod: next steps (owners): sam_sre -> collect traces + add/reduce alert thresholds; jules_eng -> schedule scheduler-tuning spike; ryan_prod -> cost/offer for small reservation; alex_c -> send customer summary & safety caveats.

novara_ops: appreciate the quick response. we'll follow up if anything else pops.

maya_oncall: assigning internal incident tag: tenant-tail-latency/novara-prod. Marking P2.

alex_c: thanks team :thumbsup: will post a short post-incident writeup after the rollout completes.

(End of thread)
